paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the cooking class. Chef Lucy waited at the door in a white hat and a white apron. "Today we are going to make fried bananas," she said. The children washed their hands at the sink. Then they put on small white aprons. On the table, there were four ingredients: bananas, flour, sugar, and a big bottle of oil.

"Shall we cut the bananas first?" asked Mia. "Let's mix the flour and water first," said Lily. "The mix needs time to rest, and we can cut the bananas after that." "Lily is right," said Chef Lucy with a smile. "A good chef thinks about time." "Why not add a lot of sugar?" asked Leo. "Let's add only a little sugar," said May, "because the bananas are already sweet." Leo laughed and put the sugar back on the table. Mia cut four bananas into long, thin pieces, and Lily put them in the mix.

The mix was ready. Chef Lucy put a pan on the cooker and poured in the oil. "The oil is very hot," she said. "Please stand back, and only I put the bananas in the pan." The pan was big and black, and the oil began to move. The children stood behind a yellow line on the floor. "My first job was in a school cafeteria," said Chef Lucy. "I cooked rice and soup for many children every day." "After that, I went to a cooking school, and now I teach here." "Cooking is my career, and I love it."

"I want a different career," said Leo. "I want to become a musician, because I like to play the drum." "Many chefs like music too," said Chef Lucy. "Shall we make some music while we cook?" asked May. Leo tapped a spoon on a bowl like a small drum, and Mia tapped two spoons on the table. The oil made a loud noise, and everybody laughed. The bananas smelled sweet, and nobody could wait.

Soon, the bananas were golden. They were ready. Chef Lucy put four pieces on a plate for each child. "These are very tasty," said Lily. "I suggest that we cook them again next month," said Leo. "Next time, you can help me in the pan," said Chef Lucy. Lily opened her notebook and wrote the steps for the blog: "First mix, then fry, last eat."

sentences.text: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the cooking class.

The children washed their hands at the sink.
Then they put on small white aprons.

"Shall we cut the bananas first?" asked Mia.
"Let's mix the flour and water first," said Lily.
"The mix needs time to rest, and we can cut the bananas after that."
"Lily is right," said Chef Lucy with a smile.
"A good chef thinks about time."
"Why not add a lot of sugar?" asked Leo.
"Let's add only a little sugar," said May, "because the bananas are already sweet."
Leo laughed and put the sugar back on the table.
Mia cut four bananas into long, thin pieces, and Lily put them in the mix.
The mix was ready.
Chef Lucy put a pan on the cooker and poured in the oil.

"Please stand back, and only I put the bananas in the pan."
The pan was big and black, and the oil began to move.
The children stood behind a yellow line on the floor.
"My first job was in a school cafeteria," said Chef Lucy.
"I cooked rice and soup for many children every day."
"After that, I went to a cooking school, and now I teach here."
"Cooking is my career, and I love it."
"I want a different career," said Leo.
"I want to become a musician, because I like to play the drum."
"Many chefs like music too," said Chef Lucy.
"Shall we make some music while we cook?" asked May.
Leo tapped a spoon on a bowl like a small drum, and Mia tapped two spoons on the table.
The oil made a loud noise, and everybody laughed.
The bananas smelled sweet, and nobody could wait.
Soon, the bananas were golden. They were ready.
Chef Lucy put four pieces on a plate for each child.
"These are very tasty," said Lily.
"I suggest that we cook them again next month," said Leo.
"Next time, you can help me in the pan," said Chef Lucy.
Lily opened her notebook and wrote the steps for the blog: "First mix, then fry, last eat."
